Speak replies: “Voice only” speaks when you asked by voice or with a wake word, not when you typed. Tap the conversation, press volume down, or say “stop” (when the wake word is on), to stop Robot talking. Show words while you speak writes down your question as you talk. Wait before answering: how long Robot waits after you stop talking before it answers; a shorter pause doesn't end your question. Hold the mic button and Robot keeps listening until you let go.

Hear you while Robot talks. Echo cancellation, the default: while Robot talks the microphone switches to the phone's call mode with echo cancellation, so “stop” and your wake words get through, and back to the best mode for questions when Robot is done. Off: the old way, the microphone hears Robot over you; tap the conversation or press the volume key to stop it. Always echo cancellation: call mode with echo cancellation the whole time the panel is open, no switching, questions a little less accurate.

Interrupt sensitivity: how readily Robot hears “stop” and your wake phrases while it talks; the wake phrases' own sensitivity stays.

Volume key stops Robot: while Robot talks and the panel is on screen, the key stops Robot and doesn't change the volume. With the screen off or the panel closed it works as always.

Test voice speed loads the downloaded models and times them on a built-in recording and two fixed sentences (nothing is played or saved). The barge-in test checks what Robot hears while it talks. The Transcription check shows how well Robot writes down Québec French and English: read sentences, or say anything and fix it; scored as conversations are decoded. The voice log lists what the voice side did, for when Robot didn't respond.

Say any of these to open Robot. Each runs on the phone: the microphone stays on while Robot listens, and nothing is recorded or saved. A longer phrase wakes Robot by accident less often. Only while charging saves battery.

Robot reads a paragraph of about 20 seconds. Run the test: say “stop” or one wake phrase, once; Robot stops when it hears it, and the result says what it heard and how fast it went quiet. Count run: Robot reads to the end while you say “stop” and your wake phrases as often as you like, a few seconds apart; the result lists each one it heard. Silent run: stay quiet; it counts anything Robot hears anyway. Tricky words: stay quiet while Robot reads words like “stop” (step, steep, stamp, bus stop); it shows how often its own words fire, and how many of those are set aside. Try each mode and each interrupt sensitivity in Settings › Voice: the result says which it ran with.
